title: serving-runtime-weekly-update-kernel-kv-batching-2026-05-27
body:
Weekly update (serving runtime) - kernel work, KV cache, batching

Date: 2026-05-27
Owner: Priya Nair
Attendees: Priya, Ethan, Marisol, Connor, Amy (arch review)

Summary highlights:
- Kernel selection heuristic landed in staging (SRV-4123). Early runs show ~9-12% p99 latency improvement for long-context Llama variants when sequence length >1024.
- KV cache incremental invalidation prototype merged to a feature branch; integration tests in progress. This reduces full-cache invalidation frequency for model-rollout traffic.
- Continuous-batching changes: adaptive windowing for short requests rolled back on canary due to increased tail latency under mixed workloads; rollback plan executed and metrics stabilized.

Metrics snapshot (last 7 days):
- Overall token throughput: +3% week-over-week (steady traffic from partner sandbox)
- Average generation latency (gpt-like workloads): 78ms/token (noisy during canary)
- p99 end-to-end latency for 2048-seq Llama mix: 420ms -> improved to 380ms on staging with new kernels
- Cache hit rate (prefix KV): 61% global; 72% on high-QPS routes

Kernel work (Ethan lead):
- What we shipped: new multi-kernel selection heuristic that chooses a fused attention kernel for dense blocks and falls back to memory-optimized kernel when KV RAM > 24GB. This was gated behind a runtime flag (kernel_selection_v2).
- Results: on staging, p50 unchanged, p95 improved 6-8% for long-context eval suites. Memory footprint decreased ~3% for batch sizes >8.
- Open items: need micro-benchmarks for A10x2 and H100-p4 configs (SRV-4176). Ethan to run on Monday and post numbers.
- Risks: kernel heuristic relies on accurate KV size estimates; we observed a mis-estimate causing a fallback oscillation in one run - fixed by adding a 100ms dampening TTL.

KV cache (Marisol lead):
- Prototype for incremental invalidation: instead of invalidating entire prefix shard on model rollouts, we now track affected token ranges and issue targeted tombstones. In tests this reduces cache churn by ~45% during canary rollouts.
- Invalidation event flow: rollout -> diff model tokenizer/embedding dims -> compute affected prefix ranges -> mark tombstones -> background GC. Proof-of-concept committed to feature branch kv/incremental-invalidate.
- Integration blockers: background GC currently competes with real-time eviction logic causing temporary memory spikes on heavy write workloads. Connor investigating LRU pressure interactions.
- Next steps: add rate-limiter for GC and make tombstone compaction incremental. Target: finish rate-limiter + tests by 2026-06-03.

Batching and scheduling (Connor lead):
- Canary rollback notes: adaptive-window batching increased batching window for short requests which improved throughput but unexpectedly increased p99 on mixed small+medium latency workloads due to head-of-line blocking.
- Immediate action: revert adaptive-window changes on canary; we did a config flip on 2026-05-25 which restored p99 to baseline.
- Work in progress: scheduler-level prioritization to avoid H/0 blocking - prototype scheduler will give preference to requests with <128 tokens and a bounded max-wait time. Early simulations show p99 improvements without throughput loss.
- Tests to run: long-running load tests with mixed QPS (10/60/300ms request distributions) scheduled for Wednesday.

Operational / Reliability:
- Observability: added per-route KV hit-rate and tombstone rate to the console dashboard. Early dashboards show high tombstone concentration on experimental routes - flagging product for follow-up.
- Incidents: a minor surge on 2026-05-22 caused elevated evictions; postmortem draft created (linked SRV-4201). Root cause: simultaneous rollouts on two services caused overlapping invalidations.

Action items / owners:
- Ethan: run micro-benchmarks on A10x2 and H100-p4, post results in SRV-4176 (due 2026-06-01).
- Marisol: implement GC rate-limiter and incremental compaction for KV tombstones; add unit/integration tests (due 2026-06-03).
- Connor: finish scheduler prioritization prototype and run mixed workload simulations (due 2026-06-02).
- Priya: coordinate canary plan for kernel_selection_v2 with SRE; prepare rollback checklist and automated metric alerts (due 2026-06-01).

Meeting notes / standup logs (this week):
- Mon 2026-05-25 standup: discussed kernel micro-bench discrepancies; decided to add dampening TTL for kernel selection.
- Tue 2026-05-26 sync with SRE: confirmed canary flipback process and alert thresholds.
- Wed 2026-05-27 arch review: Amy requested documented safety checks for kernel heuristics and guaranteed no-oscillation behavior; assigned to Ethan.

Risks / open questions:
- How will tombstone growth interact with long-tail customer sessions? Need to model worst-case prefix churn.
- Should kernel heuristic be enabled by default for Dedicated customers? Proposal: opt-in for next two weeks, then evaluate metrics for a bulk rollout.

Notes to self / work-in-progress snippets:
- Reminder: add a short-run regression test that injects model rollout events and measures cache hit-rate delta.
- TODO: update runbook to include KV GC rate-limiter knobs and alert thresholds.

Attachments / references:
- Linked artifacts: SRV-4123 (kernel heuristic), SRV-4176 (benchmarks), PR #678 (kernel heuristic), kv/incremental-invalidate branch, SRV-4201 postmortem.

If anything needs immediate attention ping #serving-runtime on Slack or DM me (Priya).
